articles.title: 'I Think That Was a Big Flaw' — Uncharted 3 Designer Says the Game Was Hindered by Too Many Set Pieces
articles.summary: An ex-Naughty Dog designer believes that Uncharted 2's success may have negatively impacted the way Uncharted 3 was developed.
articles.body:
An ex-Naughty Dog designer believes that Uncharted 2's success may have negatively impacted the way Uncharted 3 was developed.

When speaking with FRVR , ex-Naughty Dog designer Benson Russell revealed that Uncharted 2's over-the-top setpieces may have negatively impacted Uncharted 3. He noted that the big set pieces, such as the train sequence, all came organically when producing the game, but that wasn't the case for Uncharted 3. Instead, the team came up with 10 or 12 set pieces, such as the cargo plane sequence, and came up with a plan to decide on a small handful that would actually make it into the game at a later date.

Unfortunately, that never happened, and almost all of them made it into the final product. As a result, writer and director Amy Hennig was forced into a situation where she had to write all of these big set pieces into the game because the designers had already started working on them.

Uncharted Games in (Chronological) Order

“It also kind of corners Amy [Hennig] a bit, right?” he said. “Because it’s like, ‘Oh, these are the set pieces we want to do’, and she’s like, ‘Well, now I have to find a way to shoehorn the ship in, so I guess we’ll have pirates and they’ll have a pirate leader.'"

Russell went on to say that he believes making the game in this way was "a big flaw." Uncharted 3 sold exceptionally well and was highly reviewed, even scoring a 10/10 from IGN at the time . However, it does rank lower on the list when compared to other games in the series. The cargo plane sequence, however, is a standout moment that even made its way into the Uncharted live-action film a decade later.

Naughty Dog concluded the Uncharted series back in 2016, but there are rumors that the studio is returning for Uncharted 5 soon . Although its only announced title is Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, Naughty Dog has confirmed that it has multiple projects in the works. As for when we'll start to see those other games, it's hard to say, but it wouldn't be surprising if they follow Intergalatic in a relatively rapid succession.

articles.title: Silent Hill Producer Says Konami Wants to Release a New Game in the Series Every Year
articles.summary: Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto says that Konami is gunning for annual releases of new games in its flagship horror franchise.
articles.body:
Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto says that Konami is gunning for annual releases of new games in its flagship horror franchise.

Okamoto divulged this news in an interview with Gamesradar at Gamescom 2026, explaining that Konami is looking for fresh takes on the well-trodden beats of the Silent Hill series to keep it from stagnating.

"Our aim is to, hopefully, have an annual release of new games," he told the outlet. “If we stay laser-focused on the same American setting, that would exhaust [narrative] possibilities, and also potentially cause fatigue for the playerbase."

Okamoto also confirmed that several unannounced Silent Hill projects are currently in development. "There are still many projects that are still [in] the works and very unannounced titles. So obviously, we can't go into specifics. But there are still many projects that we are currently exploring and working on as we speak,” he said.

"We would like to let players know that we have more experiences coming up, and many types of games that, we believe, will be able to provide positive kinds of surprises for players waiting for this for the series."

This information holds up with statements made by Konami’s president, Hideki Hayakawa, who said the company is actively invested in “rebooting” its most iconic IPs, specifically mentioning Silent Hill, Metal Gear , and Castlevania. (Though, in this case, the word 'reboot' seems to mean reinvigorating the franchises with new games, rather than remaking old ones.)

“Our company has been making games for more than 50 years, and we hold several IPs that are beloved globally by many fans. We concluded that rebooting these properties would be an effective way to make the most of them,” he said in an interview with Nikkei Gaming on July 23. “In addition to Metal Gear, Silent Hill, and Momotaro Dentetsu, we are also actively developing Castlevania (known in Japan as Akumajō Dracula).

“Our basic philosophy is that as long as there are customers for a given game, we will release it across multiple devices. Rather than focusing intensely on just one specific IP, we’ve built a structure that allows us to push forward on multiple IPs simultaneously with equal energy. That’s what this past year has looked like for us,” he explained.

Silent Hill has enjoyed a second wind with the Silent Hill 2 Remake and Silent Hill f, alongside the upcoming Silent Hill: Townfall , set to release on September 22. Silent Hill f , specifically, seems in line with Konami’s goals for the series, taking a drastic shift from its usual American setting in favor of 1960s Japan.

For more Silent Hill news, check out the official cast reveal trailer for Silent Hill Townfall and keep an eye out on our coverage from this year’s Gamescom .

articles.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Opens Up on Future of Physical Games for Next Generation Console Project Helix
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.
articles.body:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.

Speaking with the BBC in August 2026, Sharma didn’t give a straight answer; instead, she said Xbox is currently focused on making its next generation hardware cost-effective and efficient.

“This next generation, we have to be thinking about efficiency and affordability alongside performance," she told the outlet.

Xbox Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition

"All of the industry needs to start to innovate on affordability and efficiency," she continued. "That is something that we have not had to do. But with the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console."

While she couldn’t outright confirm or deny the existence of a disc drive for Project Helix, Sharma is well-aware of the current debate surrounding physical media, and assured the BBC that she wants to give players a choice when it comes to how they choose to purchase content.

"I know players love physical media, and I know there's a lot of benefits in digital media, and I want to make sure people have a choice. There are stacks of games on everybody's shelves,” she said.

Although it wasn’t exactly a clear answer, her statement does give a positive impression of Xbox’s future plans for physical games — something the brand is already winning points for , having recently confirmed an initiative that will allow players to digitize their physical games into an online library.

First leaked earlier this summer , Xbox officially announced its disc-to-digital program on August 26 during Gamescom, which will roll out for Xbox Insiders starting on August 31 before becoming available to all players at an as-yet unconfirmed date.

This makes Xbox — which recently underwent one of the most significant restructurings in the company’s history — look pretty good in comparison to PlayStation, whose decision to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028 has unsurprisingly turned out to be quite unpopular.

Disgruntled gamers are taking to the comments section of every social media post from the company to spread awareness about the ordeal, but Sony isn’t alone — GTA 6 , the most highly-anticipated game in recent memory, is also forgoing a physical disc in favor of a digital code inside a disc case. Developer Rockstar has stood firm in its decision to bypass an actual disc, with Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick saying discs “don’t really make sense for the consumer.”

For now, it's anyone's guess as to what Project Helix will end up looking like when it comes to physical game discs, but previous reporting has hinted that it will likely be fully digital .

articles.title: Andrew Garfield’s The Uprising Sends Mixed Signals on Robin Hood Connection
articles.summary: Focus Features’ The Uprising stars Andrew Garfield in a 1381 Peasants' Revolt drama—but new marketing suggests it might actually be a stealth Robin Hood origin story.
articles.body:
Focus Features’ The Uprising stars Andrew Garfield in a 1381 Peasants' Revolt drama—but new marketing suggests it might actually be a stealth Robin Hood origin story.

“To the rich, he was an outlaw. To the people, he was a hero. Witness the rise of Robin Hood in The Uprising, only in theaters September 11,” according to this post from the film’s official X account . Until this point in the publicity campaign, none of the movie’s marketing materials revealed any such ties to the iconic outlaw.

This ad revealed the film’s new title as The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood. It shows Garfield’s character, dressed in a green hood, emerging from the woods to confront the King and his soldiers. He is accompanied by his fellow highwaymen, who wield bows and arrows. “There will be no peace until we are free. Time to pay,” Garfield’s character declares at swordpoint.

To the rich, he was an outlaw. To the people, he was a hero. Witness the rise of Robin Hood in THE UPRISING, only in theaters September 11. — The Uprising (@theuprisingmov) August 20, 2026

To the rich, he was an outlaw. To the people, he was a hero. Witness the rise of Robin Hood in THE UPRISING, only in theaters September 11.

A day after this ad was released the film’s title was changed back to being just The Uprising.

The film’s UK distributor even released a statement denying The Uprising is a Robin Hood movie (via Metro ): “Marketing materials posted by other countries that may appear in the UK online and on social media referencing Robin Hood are not issued or approved by us.”

The Uprising had been understood to be about the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, which was led by historical figures Wat Tyler (played by Shogun’s Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (played by Jamie Bell). Garfield’s character Ploughman was thought to represent the Everyman peasant pushed by misfortune into taking up arms against the crown.

The Uprising’s original US production notes – made available in advance to stateside press for the film’s junket – did not reveal any ties to Robin Hood. Garfield’s character was referred to as merely Ploughman. The original plot synopsis read:

“Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.”

But the latest production notes, released to US press late last week, contained this updated synopsis : “Andrew Garfield stars as the leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. Set against the true events of the Uprising that helped inspire the legend of Robin Hood, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice.”

These same updated US production notes later state: “The 14th century English poem ‘Piers Plowman’ — a simple farmer’s dream about his hopes and fears — was the inspiration for the character of the Ploughman and helped the filmmaker [Paul Greengrass] settle on his approach. (Notably, the same poem gave birth to the legend of ‘Robin Hoode,’ the ultimate British outlaw myth about a common man attempting to right great injustice and coming under threat from the authorities for his actions to serve the citizenry.)”

The Most Famous Movie and TV Characters Who've Met Robin Hood

With The Uprising just a few short weeks away from theatrical release, any such conflicting messaging about what the film’s about risks confusing or turning off potential audiences.

If The Uprising is indeed a Robin Hood film then it will arrive on the heels of the Hugh Jackman-starring The Death of Robin Hood , a box office bomb that grossed less than $7 million worldwide against a reported production budget of $20 million.

articles.title: The 10 Most Expensive MTG Cards in The Hobbit Set
articles.summary: Here are the most valuable cards in the Magic: The Gathering x The Hobbit set.
articles.body:
For all of the controversy around Magic: The Gathering’s Universes Beyond sets, we imagine a lot of people were very excited for a return to Middle-Earth when The Hobbit was announced.

Now, ahead of launch, we’re still wondering where those Commander Decks are, but we can console ourselves with some absolutely awesome artwork and some really cool new cards.

Gleaming Splendor (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

The Arkenstone (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Smaug, Wicked Worm (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Gandalf, Goblins' Bane (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Bard, King of Dale (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Smaug the Magnificent (Showcase) (Surge Foil)

Thorin, Mountain-king (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Thranduil, the Elvenking (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

The Queen of Dale (Showcase) (Surge Foil)

Before we cover the set’s priciest cards, we’re going via TCGplayer pricing, and there’s no amount attached to the One Ring just yet.

The Most Valuable Cards In The Hobbit’s Magic: The Gathering Set

10 - Smaug, Wicked Worm (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $120

It wouldn’t be a Hobbit list without Smaug, and he’ll appear again, don’t you worry. This version of Smaug is a five-cost flying dragon that creates X tapped treasure tokens where X is the number of artifacts your opponents control.

Paying mana costs with treasure then nets you card draw, at the cost of 1 life each time. This covetous dragon is going for around $120.

9 - Bard, King of Dale (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $140

Slightly pricier than Smaug is the Borderless, Surge Foil treatment of Bard, King of Dale . A six-cost 3/5 with reach and vigilance, it doubles your card draw outside of draw steps, and doubles up counters, too.

You can get this version for around $140 at the time of writing, and it’s actually climbing.

8 - Thorin, Mountain-king (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $150

Another book cover, Thorin, Mountain-King is core to the story of The Hobbit, and this Dwarf Noble attaches equipment to one of your creatures for free.

When one or more pieces of equipment become attached to that creature this way, that creature deals damage equal to its power to up to one target creature. It’s also a 3/4 body with Trample, and is selling for around $150.

7 - Thranduil, the Elvenking (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $160

Another book cover treatment, Thranduil, the Elvenking is a 5/6 that has all activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard.

It also allows you to draw cards and discard a card when another legendary Elf enters, making it ideal for typal synergies — and green and blue have a ton of access to Elves. It’s around $160.

6 - The Queen of Dale (Showcase) (Surge Foil) - $180

Kicking off our list, this version of The Queen of Dale is sitting at $180 and lets you recruit when your opponents cast noncreature spells.

Recruit, you say? This mechanic allows you to draw and discard a card, creating a 1/1 white Human Soldier token if you discard a nonland card. You can swiftly ramp up your side of the board (and your graveyard) if you’re recruiting for every noncreature spell, especially at a cost of just two mana.

5 - Smaug the Magnificent (Borderless) - $200

One of the most striking visuals in the set, Smaug the Magnificent’s borderless treatment is going for around $200.

It doesn’t say it on this version of the card, but this card deals damage equal to the number of Treasures you control to any target, be that a creature or a player. And, at the beginning of your upkeep, you get a Treasure token, too. All of that, plus it’s a 4/3 with flying and haste.

4 - Gandalf, Goblins' Bane (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $250

Gandalf, Goblins' Bane was always going to be popular, but this version of the iconic Wizard is useful, too. Not only can he be cast as a 2/3 Avatar Wizard who gains +1/+1 with noncreature spells and pings opponents for damage, but he can act as a Sorcery, too.

Flameshape lets you exile two cards from your library and play them as long as you control a Wizard. He’s close to breaking the $250 mark with this book cover version.

3 - The Arkenstone (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $300

The MacGuffin before the One Ring, The Arkenstone is a Legendary Artifact that powers up your creatures and nets you end-of-turn card draw.

You can play it as a Sorcery, too, which lets you search for a legendary creature card and put it into your hand. It’s $305 right now.

2 - Smaug the Magnificent (Showcase) (Surge Foil) - $310

More Smaug, anyone? Functionally the same as the version mentioned above, this version shows the fearsome dragon napping on a pile of gold and treasure.

1 - Gleaming Splendor (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $1000

Going to the $1000 mark is Gleaming Splendor , an Enchantment that gets you Treasure Tokens as players draw their second card on a turn.

As the artwork suggests, this pairs nicely with Smaug, The Magnificent if you’re playing red and white, and you can even pay additional mana to force other players to draw a card. It’s $1000 right now.

IGN reached out to Tor and Bethesda for clarification on this, and we've been told that the "free copy of [The Elder Scrolls Online] is on the whole first print run" and thus is "available from all retailers, including Amazon" in the UK.

For those who prefer to shop local, participating bookshops are also handing out branded bookmarks containing a secondary code that unlocks a "Pink Torchbug" pet for use in ESO as well.

After purchasing the novel, readers can enter the codes printed on the sticker through Tor's redemption page to claim the game , limited to the first 10,000 sign-ups.

Announcing the collaboration with Bethesda, Tor described it as a partnership for "cosy fantasy book lovers and gamers", encouraging readers to move from Baldree's latest story into creating their own adventure in Tamriel.

The Elder Scrolls Online remains one of Bethesda, and now Xbox's, biggest ongoing titles more than a decade after launch, continuing to receive expansions and regular content updates while attracting new players through subscription services, sales, and now, apparently, bookshops.

Fans have also recently been reassured by Zenimax and Microsoft that, despite a recent round of layoffs across Xbox, ESO will continue and isn't on the verge of being shut down.

Bethesda is also continuing to support its other big IP, Fallout. Remasters of Fallout 3 and New Vegas are in the works in addition to a new Fallout game from Obsidian Entertainment. Bethesda has also entered pre-production on Fallout 5 , likely to ensure the team can make the jump to it after The Elder Scrolls 6 is finished.

The modder confirmed that "almost all in-game characters, monsters, animals, vegetation, armors, and equipment for Geralt and Roach," as well as "a large part of the environment," have been reworked for The Witcher 3 Remastered. They added, "I've put a lot of effort into ensuring the highest quality. :)"

The Witcher 3 Remastered was officially announced at gamescom Opening Night Live (ONL) 2026. articles.title: ‘We Have To Be Careful’ — Rockstar on GTA 6’s Approach to Satire
articles.summary: Rockstar is still dedicated to making Grand Theft Auto a funny satire of modern America, but it’s being careful with its references to ensure GTA 6 doesn’t feel dated before it launches.
articles.body:
Thirteen years is a long time. It can feel especially long when you’re developing a game in a series that loves nothing more than to satirize the times we live in. GTA 6 has the challenge, then, of not feeling out of touch with the world its trying to find the funny side of.

It’s something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North is astutely aware. “That’s a question a lot of people ask: how do you deal with satire in today’s world?” he told IGN on an exclusive visit to the developer’s Scottish office.

“I think there’s always stuff to satirize. As long as humans are humans, other humans will figure out ways to satirize what we do. For us, because we work on such a long development cycle, we have to not jump on stuff and instead choose our angle of approach carefully and decide what things are going to be a bit more timeless. We’re not a TV show coming out every week or every month. We have to be careful that what we’re choosing to satirize is not going to feel dated in a weird way. I think those broader things are OK to satirize, but very specific political issues or memes will date fast. Even the way our characters speak we think about it a lot, so that they're not using extremely contemporary slang. Even though our characters are a certain age, they need to feel somewhat timeless.”

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

Being able to feel a connection with the two protagonists is a huge part of Rockstars’s games. They are, typically, people commits crimes and doing horrible things to one another, so creating a warmth toward them is a real challenge. This is something that Rockstar has decades of experience doing by now, though. Making sure they feel true-to-life when talking, and giving them believable, and somewhat relatable backgrounds is a huge part of this.

“Jason and Lucia as characters have rich backstories that we sometimes explicitly talk about, sometimes just allude to,” Nelson reveals. “I think there is enough detail there if you want to pay attention, but we also have purposely left them with some room for interpretation so that hopefully the connection can be enhanced between the player and these characters. That is maybe as important as it has ever been for these characters in particular because I think for this story to work for you, for you to buy into this relationship, you have to be able to connect with them in some way. Hopefully a good number of people will feel like they can do that.”

Satire, nor characters, are the aspects that Rockstar settles on first when developing a new Grand Theft Auto game, though. The origin point is the world, and, in the case of GTA 6, a return to Vice City.

“A lot of people ask how do you think about satire and what angle to use? But satire is not usually the first thing that we think about, it’s something that develops,” Nelson explains. “The first thing we think about is where are we going to set it? – OK, Miami and Florida – Vice City and Leonida. Then we go there and start meeting with as many different people as we can. We start figuring out what sorts of experiences we want the player to have, and what places we want them to go, and what types of people we want them to meet. Then we figure out what’s a good character set to take the player through that? Those are the big things. Then, we ask, ‘What do we want to improve upon that we did before?’ Certainly choice. Another big thing is trying to connect who you are in the narrative with who you are in the open world as much as possible, so it feels like one singular experience.”

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Rockstar Doesn’t Mind if You Dislike GTA 6’s Romantic Side: ‘Don’t Bother With It. Up to You’
articles.summary: GTA 6 has a whole relationship system to increase Jason and Lucia’s bond, but it’s completely optional if you’d rather keep things platonic.
articles.body:
During an interview with IGN, Rob Nelson, the head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, explained the design decisions behind making Jason and Lucia's relationship key to the story but not to the gameplay mechanics.

"I have to say it feels great — if you are into it as a concept. Don’t bother with it if you aren’t. Up to you," said Nelson. Jason and Lucia will always have each other's backs in the story and during the action, but spending quality time together and nurturing the relationship? That's up to the player, and you won't be penalized if you're not interested in the sappy stuff.

"The narrative is structured in such a way that the circumstances they find themselves in require them to stay together for most of the story and work together. At the very least they will get through most things as partners in crime," explained Nelson.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

"I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us. Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."

For players that want to spend time together, the vast map of Leonida offers plenty of opportunities for the quality time Nelson mentioned.

"Robbing places together, or walking around, holding hands, going to a zoo, studying animals, going scuba diving, parachuting, walking on the beach, kayaking…," he said.

"When you bring them together, it feels like you’re a steward of their relationship, and you feel protective of them as a unit. But this is something we did not know when we started, and it really had to be something we felt our way through. But I will say that whether you’re getting in trouble, or you’re running from the cops, or getting in a car, or waiting for the other one — playing as them together feels very cool. It feels like you’re taking care of them, if that’s something you’re into."

Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on November 19.

She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: ‘It’s a Step Forward in All Respects’ – Exclusive GTA 6 Interview
articles.summary: Our exclusive interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson reveals how GTA 6 aims to be “a step forward in all respects.”
articles.body:
The whole world is going feral as Grand Theft Auto 6's November release date approaches, desperate for even the tiniest of details. Meanwhile Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, is a man who has had to keep all those details secret for a very long time.

Finally, when I sat down in his office in the Scottish capital of Edinburgh for an exclusive IGN interview, he was able to spill some of those GTA 6 secrets for the very first time.

"I think the challenge for us on this game is the same as it is on any new game for us,” says Nelson. “How do we evolve and build upon the good things we have done before in all the ways these things need to evolve, but at the same time ensure that the game still has everything that made the previous games in this series resonate with people?"

The answer seems to be, for a large (if not the most) part, in creating a whole world that players can spend meaningful time in, engaging in fulfilling activities that go beyond simply grinding sidequests for cash or trying to boost stats to power through the main story. The setting of Leonida is begging to be explored and experienced by the player.

"The game is so big, I don’t know that there’s anybody on the team that knows all of it," he says.

As we're talking, Nelson is multitasking, playing through a slice of Grand Theft Auto 6 that will go on to perfectly exemplify his point. It's dense with NPCs, traffic weaving through the streets, and opportunities for mayhem at every turn. And those people on the sidewalks? They're ready to cause all sorts of chaos.

"While we pushed interaction with NPCs as far as we could for Red Dead Redemption 2, with this game we are taking it much further,” he explains. "The team has done an incredible job to create all of this crazy dialogue, and you can stand there and listen to them, but we’ve tried to find a balance where if you stand too close to a group, they should notice that you're eavesdropping."

"So, if you stand there and try to listen to the whole thing, they'll often turn around, notice you and go, ‘Oh hey, can I help you?’ Or if you follow people for too long and too close so that they can hear you, they’ll go, ‘Oh, hey.’ Then they may be aggressive, or they may just want to get away from you. When we first started these ideas back on Red Dead Redemption 2, we thought if we could get it working there in a more sparsely populated world, we imagined what it might feel like at scale in a modern world. So it was one of the scary but very worthwhile and fun challenges we took on with this game."

According to Nelson, an epic amount of time, research and work went into populating the world, styling the NPCs so that every area of the world feels distinct. Rockstar even had a team in LA solely dedicated to NPC dialogue, which is how you end up with GTA gems like "you can use my balls like a punching bag" and "I can pee on you if you pay me."

The evolution of the world’s NPCs extend beyond banter, clothing, and mugging them for $5. It's one of the places where it’s clear that the development of Red Dead Redemption 2 has had a significant influence on GTA 6.

"This NPC interaction system is one that is returning and evolved from Red Dead Redemption 2,” says Nelson. “In the past, we’ve had systems where you can speak to NPCs, in Red Dead Redemption 1 and GTA 5 there were basic systems for interacting, but the interactions were very simple. But with Red Dead Redemption 2, we were finally able to incorporate the ability to interact with NPCs as a more fleshed-out system."

He specifically references the use of the left trigger, something that was once a binary system, and how the team had to adapt to allow for the more nuanced approach of using the trigger as a way to interact with the world without pulling out a weapon. That same system and the expertise around it have made their way into GTA 6.

"We have to do so much work in design, in code behaviors, in animation, in writing, to get these

interactions to feel believable," he says. "Now, everybody across all of these teams – across technical teams, animation teams, across design teams, across writing teams – need to in a way become students of human behavior. You find yourself watching how people behave out in the world and studying the rise and fall of a conversation as you pass two people."

That detail and the specificity it allows for is supported by the new Criminal Profile system, a spiritual successor to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor system. While it does dynamically alter based on activities that could be broadly considered “good” or “bad”, your profile is not there to encourage you to be a perfect citizen. This is a game about how much fun it can be to break the law, after all, but it’s up to you how maliciously violent you want to be about it.

"As much as possible, we tried to design the game so that you have options,” Nelson explains. “Things can escalate quite quickly if you want them to, or people who don’t want to escalate can try to avoid it. It’s not always possible. To me that supports the narrative.

"This is a story about a couple on the run. We have tried to make the systems and the design support our narrative when and wherever possible. Meaning, if you hit and run, commit a crime and run, get into trouble and move on before the cops get there, and you don’t start shooting people, don't start escalating – which you absolutely can do if you want to – but if you don’t, you’re generally going to be fine."

Nelson says the team began to experiment with the idea that you're not the only dangerous person in the world in Red Dead Redemption 2. In its lawless frontier you could be attacked by roving gangs, or start fights with people on the trails. GTA 6 builds new layers into those choices.

"So, if you're doing things on mission that you are required to do – or you’re robbing places, or somebody comes and messes with you and you have to deal with them by smacking them down or whatever – that’s all fair game,” Nelson explains. “It's when you go beyond what is necessary on a consistent basis, or you do completely unnecessary stuff consistently, that you may start to sway your criminal profile in a certain direction."

"Maybe you care about that as a player, maybe you don’t. There is no right or wrong way to play this. To us, it's a very interesting concept. In previous games, you’re quite overpowered in the world compared to everyone else apart from the cops, which can be fun, but not as fun, I don’t think, as having a world where there may be other people that have impulses of their own and act upon you. You are still powerful and capable, but you are not the only one capable of violence or the only one with weapons or the only crazy person out there. It makes the world far more unpredictable and interesting."

This new system exists alongside the iconic Wanted levels and risk of getting Busted. Again, further complexity has been added to these systems, but the same thrills of evading police helicopters, fleeing mayhem in sports cars, and getting into deeper and deeper trouble at every turn are still alive and well.

"The Wanted system in GTA 6 requires that someone witness the crime, or an alarm needs to be set off for it to be reported to the law," explains Nelson. "One star is not going to be too difficult to get away from. You can see with these little icons on-screen, the police know what we're driving, so we should just jump out of the vehicle. They also know we're a couple. You could split up, and that will also help lower the police’s perception of you."

The same goes for swapping to a different vehicle during a chase or even just changing clothes and pulling on a baseball cap. The key to getting away won't always be a fast car, though; the busy roads of the more built-up areas of Leonida mean sometimes fleeing on foot will be the way to go.

"We put a lot of work into how you can navigate the world, trying to make everything as smooth as possible to really encourage this type of gameplay where you are running and getting out of the car, jumping and climbing fences. If you get three stars in the city, it can sometimes be challenging to get away in a vehicle, unless it's a very fast vehicle or a sports bike. Your best option is usually to do this—get off the streets and get on foot into the alleys."

One of the many ways to stir up trouble is the titular grand theft auto, and that's still a major part of the action. The gameplay we saw included breaking into a police impound lot in search of a particular sports car a quest-giver had requested. As a higher-value vehicle, it also allowed Nelson to explain some of the changes Rockstar has made to the process of boosting cars.

"We have put some layers of stratification into the vehicles,” he says. “Previously, you could just press triangle to automatically hotwire and steal any vehicle that you wanted and take off. We felt like that left a lot of potential gameplay on the table in terms of progression and decision-making for players," he said. "So now, you start off the game and there are certain parked cars that are not accessible to you until you get a bit further along with the story and you acquire certain tools to get into them, but you can always carjack any driver you see."

"We also now have this scanner as a part of the phone,” says Nelson. From the brief glimpse we caught of it in the gameplay demo, it appears to be an app called, delightfully, Waink. Scanning a car with Waink will spit out a number of facts. “For example, it tells me this car is locked, it's got an alarm, and has no tracker. It also tells me how much it’s worth if I go to take it to a Pay n’ Spray or a specialty car fence, and how much it would cost for me to register it for myself. So, for example, this car needs a key cloner. This other car will just need a Slim Jim. So we’ve added a lot of fun little tools you need or mechanics you need to perform these formerly binary actions."

Ultimately, it all comes down to choice. Rockstar has created a romance, a story, and a rich and immersive world, but what you do with them is up to you.

"We are always trying to find that balance between freedom and storytelling," explains Nelson. "It is a challenge, and sometimes when you are trying to create a specific or hopefully compelling narrative, the narrative aspect does need to take precedence at times – at least for us it does. To move the narrative forward in a believable way, you have to hit these beats, and so in those cases we have to kind of guide the experience. But with this game we have made a very conscious effort to open things up where possible – without compromising the quality of the experience."

Of course, that means things won't always go to plan, whether you're a player firing up the game in November or Nelson himself, getting Wasted because a car sideswiped him while he was trying to escape the cops.

"We are very excited about some of what we have going on now in the open world, with how it reacts to you and the systems we have working together. We have a lot of emergent natural-feeling stuff happening pretty often now as you roam around the world. That was truly emergent for me, when we drove past that car park and Jason suggested we do that job – I hadn’t actually heard that dialogue from him myself yet. And it worked – I was going to a pawn shop, then Jason said, ‘Should we go do this?’ as we drove by, and I changed my mind.

"And one of the coolest things in GTA 6 is how much fun it can be to be with your partner,” Nelson continues. “You’ll have seen it in the [Extended Look video], and it will be interesting to see if people pick up on it. Because, yes, the video showcases three pretty action-heavy missions intercut with loads of other things you can do, but in just one little sequence we show a couple of robberies, which represents a huge amount of what you can and need to be doing in this game in between story missions."

That's the other big change for GTA 6. You've been able to swap between multiple protagonists in a GTA game before, but this time around you can swap between Jason and Lucia, and nurture their relationship as its own specific unit.

"There is a system that tracks what sort of criminal you are. And then there is also a relationship system,” explains Nelson. “They're separate. You manage the relationship in the way you hopefully nurture any relationship – which is by spending time together. So being in the open world and exploring together or doing activities together, playing pool or mini golf or kayaking; normal slice of life things. Or, robbing stores together, robbing banks together. However players want to spend that time together, it will have a positive impact on the relationship."

When you're out in the world solo, you can stay in touch with your partner over text, checking in to say goodnight or asking them to come and meet you. The way Nelson describes it, there’s all the drama you expect from a Grand Theft Auto story, but with a very authentic relationship at the heart of it.

"With the relationship, we start Jason and Lucia off wanting to give it a shot, but just going through the story and playing missions together may not be enough to keep them together,” Nelson warns. “You’ll have to keep them together by spending a bit of time together in the open world, and then hopefully that will reinforce your connection to them and increase your investment in their story." said Nelson.

While Jason and Lucia’s relationship extends out of the story and into GTA’s mechanical systems, he also pointed out that you can decide not to work on your relationship without negatively affecting the experience.

"The narrative is structured in such a way that the circumstances they find themselves in require them to stay together for most of the story and work together. At the very least they will get through most things as partners in crime,” Nelson explains. “I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us. Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."

And while you'll almost certainly be drawn to one character or another - I love Lucia's badass personality, but perhaps you’ll be more drawn to Jason's golden retriever with a gun energy - Rockstar has made a conscious effort to make sure it wasn't playing favorites when it came to the characters.

"As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character. After doing GTA 5, we talked about different ideas of – do we do more characters? How do we follow up three characters? Is it four characters now? But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each and, therefore, player connection with those characters. So we decided to step in this direction of two characters in a relationship.

“But then the question became, 'How do you make players feel like, ‘I love them both?’ Chemistry is a notoriously hard thing to do in any sort of entertainment. Either the characters and the actors that embody them have it – or they don't. Everyone involved worked at that pretty hard. I think we’ve got it. I think we’ve got enough reaction within our team internally to where they feel great as individuals and together."

I met with Nelson a month before the new ‘Extended Look’ video dropped, which has offered us all the biggest insight into the game so far, so I had to ask what Rockstar is hoping for from fans and how much pressure the team felt after generating so much anticipation for so long.

"I try not to think about it. You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what we’ve done previously, evolving it while still making it feel familiar," he said.

"As much pressure as we feel externally, I don’t think it can compare to the pressure we put on ourselves as a team. Everyone wants things to be perfect. We are nervous! Nervous, of course, but also excited to see how people respond to this video and then ultimately the game. It is definitely a step forward in all respects for us – the size of the world and how deep it feels. It’s a bit of a shock when you get in there and you see the density of the traffic, the density of population, and the fidelity of their responses to you."

That's the message I took away from the interview and what I saw. Players are going to be shocked. Shocked, like finding out your pet dog can also predict lottery results. Shocked, like finding out that you're actually the descendant of a rich guy in Budapest who died and named you in his will. While Nelson says "it's still very much Grand Theft Auto," all the additions and tweaks that I saw make it a new benchmark for open world experiences.

"There is a whole other world in Red Dead Redemption 2," Nelson says, "GTA 6 is very much like that. There's a whole lot of stuff that you discover emergently that we're not necessarily directing you to through objectives or blips or icons on a map as well. If you take a bit of time and explore you will be rewarded – a lot."

Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on November 19.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: Here's Every Song Featured in Rockstar's GTA 6 Extended Look
articles.summary: Rockstar Games' first official extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 featured a lot of licensed music, and we've got the list of every song it featured right here.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games' first official extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 featured a lot of licensed music, and we've got the list of every song it featured right here.

Grand Theft Auto games are known for having killer soundtracks, and GTA 6 will be no different. That much was clear from today's 26-minute gameplay debut, with tracks from rock, rap, and everything in between shown off.

We watched the big Netflix reveal along with everyone else and managed to catch the full list of tracks for your listening pleasure. You can see every song featured in the GTA 6 extended look below.

Let Your Love Flow – The Bellamy Brothers

But I Think It's a Dream – Captain & Tennille

Off the Grid – Chk Chk Chk (!!!) (feat. Meah Pace)

Se Me Nota (Agarrame) Prod by B-One – Chimbala, Omega

Against All Odds (Take a Look at Me Now) – Phil Collins

Of course, the GTA 6 extended look had a lot more than music to show off, too. This preview of what 13 years of waiting will give players also came with a fresh look at a smorgasbord of side activities , shootouts, car chases, and story moments to sink our teeth into, too.

Another update for the long-awaited sixth Grand Theft Auto game includes the promise that a story playthrough will be about 80 hours long . IGN also got an early sneak peek, so be sure to check out our preview and interview .

Protagonists Jason and Lucia will have plenty to listen to when GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. For more, you can check out everything revealed during the big reveal showcase here .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: GTA VI looks just as great as we could hope for
articles.summary: Netflix and Rockstar Games just wrapped up their big “extended look” at Grand Theft Auto VI, and it featured a bunch of story scenes and showed how it will keep much of the spirit of GTA.
articles.body: Netflix and Rockstar Games finally debuted their “extended look” at Grand Theft Auto VI. It showed that the new game looks to keep much of the spirit of GTA — exploration, driving, crimes, shooting, and cinematic story scenes. But everything just looks much better than previous entries, with impressive graphics, densely-packed rooms, and detailed environments. The footage was captured on PS5, according to the end of the video. A key focus of the game seems to be how protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos work together. In one scene, it appears you play as Duval as he hangs out of the window of a car that Caminos is driving so he can shoot at police chasing after them. Later, though, it looks like the player controls Caminos as the driver while Duval and another character keep shooting the police. Another part of the video shows a mission where Duval and Caminos are split up. As enemies barge into an upper floor of a building, Duval, who is a security detail for the mission, takes them on by hiding behind cover and shooting at them. Caminos, who is on a different floor, sneaks around on foot to try and evade detection. At one point, while she is struggling on the ground against an enemy, you can see button prompts to press to escape their grasp. Much of the video included tightly-edited scenes and cutscenes from the game, but there were a few other brief glimpses of gameplay, like a weapon wheel menu and activities driving a boat, playing basketball, underwater diving, racing on a track, and parachuting. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The game appears to be quite large. As part of a preview by The New York Times, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson said that a February playthrough of the game took 80 hours, including both the main story and some optional content. The map is three times as the playable map of Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar tells the NYT. You’ll be able to switch between the two protagonists at “any time,” though you can also choose to have one character tag along while you’re running around the world or experience things as just one of them, according to IGN, which also got a preview of the game. Duval and Caminos also don’t necessarily have to be a romantic couple; that’s up to the player. (There’s a specific mechanic for holding hands.) Snapmatic, GTA’s take on Instagram, returns in GTA VI, though you can’t actually post on it “due to Jason and Lucia being a couple on the run and not wanting to leave a digital footprint,” according to IGN. The six-star wanted system is also officially back, and police can remember what you look like, meaning you may need to change outfits to lose them, IGN says. If you want to steal a parked car to get away from a sticky situation, you might want to look for an older car: more expensive cars will be harder to steal and you may need certain equipment to break into certain cars. The deep dive follows several apparent video leaks of the game from a person or group identifying themselves as “CyberLeek,” which Rockstar said were “heartbreaking.” Thursday’s extended look will be available on Rockstar’s YouTube channel and the GTA VI website at 9PM ET. The game is scheduled to release on November 19th at a starting price of $79.99, but you won’t be able to buy it on a physical disc. Update, August 27th: Added details from IGN and the NYT’s previews.
